title: Force, Mass and Acceleration in Flight
learningObjectives: Calculate acceleration from net force and mass in one dimension using a = F_net / m
Explain that acceleration is proportional to net force and inversely proportional to mass for constant mass

evidence.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.

explanations.text: Acceleration depends on both applied force and mass, expressed for constant mass as force equals mass times acceleration.

evidence.quote: The change in velocity divided by the change in time is the definition of the acceleration a.
Remember that this relation is only good for objects that have a constant mass.

explanations.text: Acceleration is change in velocity over change in time, and the mass-times-acceleration form applies when mass stays constant.

evidence.quote: If there is no net force acting on the object, then the object will maintain a constant velocity.

explanations.text: With zero net force velocity does not change; an unbalanced force is needed to accelerate an object.

behavioralTests.name: negative net force gives negative acceleration
zero net force gives zero acceleration
